relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
detail: The Bank of Lithuania's own gold reserves page states that "As much as 5.8 tons of Lithuanian gold are currently held at the Bank of England" and describes the Bank of England as the custodian for Lithuania's gold. The 5.8 tonnes comprise 466 bars; the page states that no gold is stored domestically and that the bank has no plans to change the storage location. The page adds that the gold held there is also invested through deposits or swaps, but the storage tie itself is custody.

relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
detail: Banco de la Republica's own question-and-answer page on where the international reserves are invested states: "la entidad encargada de custodiar el oro de las reservas internacionales es el Banco de Inglaterra" - the entity charged with the custody of the international reserves' gold is the Bank of England. The page gives no share or tonnage and names no other location.
source_title: Donde estan invertidas las reservas, el oro colombiano y con que entidades se negocia - Banco de la Republica

relation: holds its gold reserves in custody
detail: The gold note in Banka Slovenije's 2024 audited financial statements distinguishes "the stock of gold held at Banka Slovenije" from the remainder, described only as "gold in foreign bank accounts". The central bank therefore keeps part of its own gold on its own premises; the note names no foreign institution and gives no split by weight or value between the two locations. Total holdings at 31 December 2024 were 102,216 fine troy ounces, valued at EUR 256,671 thousand.
